segments.text: On a hot day, a dog pants with its tongue out.
But its fur never gets damp with sweat.
Dogs only have sweat glands in their paw pads.
So they can't cool off by sweating all over.
But when moisture evaporates, it carries heat away.
So a dog keeps its tongue and mouth wet with saliva.
Then it pants fast to dry that saliva quickly.
Check again - its coat is still dry.
Panting dries the wet tongue and mouth to release heat.
